explicit_validation.explanation: The paper conducts both LLM and human evaluations on the same sets of question pairs, compares their performance using accuracy metrics, and discusses the relationship between LLM and human evaluation results

prompts.notes: Step 1 and Step 2 prompts are shown in Appendix A.1, but full evaluation prompts are not provided verbatim

guidelines.notes: Annotators were given definitions of each dimension and the desirable trait R_d as specified in §4.1

sample_size.notes: 60 pairs of human-written questions and 60 pairs of machine-generated questions were evaluated by both LLM and human annotators

quantitative_scores.notes: Human performance on human-written question pairs
Human performance on distractor efficiency dimension
QG-SMS achieves second-highest accuracy overall, closest to human performance

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Not explicitly stated, but QG-SMS described as achieving 'state-of-the-art alignment with human judgment'

validation_results.summary_finding: QG-SMS shows strong alignment with human judgment, achieving the highest accuracy on generated questions and the second-highest overall, closely matching human performance on difficulty and efficiency while surpassing humans on discrimination evaluation

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluate the same three dimensions (DF, DC, DE) on the validation set, while topic coverage (TC) was only evaluated by LLM methods
